data.name: Arshaq
data.gender_notes: Arshaq is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word ‘as’ meaning ‘horse’ and ‘rah’ meaning ‘rider’ or ‘road’. Arshaq is a name of a Sassanian king who reigned from 262 to 272 AD. He is remembered for his courage, generosity, and love for horseback riding. The name Arshaq carries the meaning “Rider of a horse” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Arshaq usually hope their child will grow to embody rider of a horse and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing strength, courage, and determination in the face of challenges, inspired by the legendary king Arshaq and his love for horses.
data.etymology: Arshaq belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rider of a horse.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arshaq total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.
